id: title:eli-r-ph:stop a client timestamp panicking the request

review.posthog_relevance: Protects the Rust shared library used by PostHog's backend services against panics when parsing client-supplied timestamps, preventing request abortion and potential batch loss.
review.reason: Replaces unsafe byte slicing with safe character-boundary-aware retrieval and adds a regression test. This protects the Rust shared library used by PostHog's backend services against panics when parsing client-supplied timestamps. A panic would abort the request and potentially lose the entire batch, whereas this change returns None, allowing the caller to handle the rejection.
review.uncertainty: While the implementation and test are supplied, the exact production impact and historical incident avoidance cannot be verified from this patch alone.

observations.limitations: This chunk contains two hunks. P1.F1.H2 is a test-only addition. P1.F1.H1 is the implementation change. The implementation and its corresponding test are supplied, allowing an assessment of the tier.
